caveat: Entity-level SOC statement lines for NSW TrainLink only. Never add to government program spending, to the PNFC sector benchmark, or to each other: Total revenue (97,080 thousand) excludes the separately presented Grants and contributions line (395,366 thousand); Total expenses excluding losses (377,742 thousand) excludes the below-the-line Gains/(losses) on disposal and Impairment reversals/(losses) that are included in the printed net-result bridge; the net result is a surplus of 113,817 thousand. The annual report is branded NSW TrainLink but the audited statement is for the legal entity NSW Trains, so every row records legal_name NSW Trains and is provisional and unverified, flagged for human spot-check.
notes: Latest NSW TrainLink annual report discovered from the official Transport for NSW NSW TrainLink annual-reports page (no hard-coded PDF URL) and archived with SHA-256 outside the repo. NSW TrainLink publishes two volumes; the audited Statement of comprehensive income is in Volume 2, so discovery selects the latest report year's financial-statements volume. The statement prints an explicit $'000 unit and explicit Total revenue and Total expenses excluding losses subtotals. Both printed totals are accepted only when the printed revenue lines, expense lines, deficit-before-grants bridge, operations-result bridge (adding Grants and contributions) and net-result bridge (adding gains/losses on disposal and impairment reversals) reconcile exactly. Grants and contributions are separately disclosed in Note 2(c), so one grant row carries potential_double_count=true. The annual report is branded NSW TrainLink but the audited statement is for the legal entity NSW Trains; that provenance caveat is recorded and two lines are flagged for human spot-check. Every row is a provisional, unverified entity-level SOC statement line (jurisdiction_level=soc, aggregation_role=agency_detail); never add NSW TrainLink rows to government program spending, the PNFC benchmark, or any other SOC.
